title: Why Harvey Was Mocked
topic: Why William Harvey was mocked for saying the heart pumps blood in a circle

lines: A physician thrust his palm into a beating pigeon’s chest.
Colleagues laughed, calling his claim “a wild fantasy.”
They clung to Galen’s ancient idea that the liver spewed fresh blood.
Harvey publishes De Motu Cordis in Frankfurt.
Patients stop coming; his practice “falls mightily.”
You see, it’s like watching a bathtub drain while the faucet keeps running – the water never disappears.
Harvey measured the heart’s capacity, counted beats, and proved the volume of blood moved each half‑hour was far too great for the liver to produce.
His experiments on fish and serpents showed veins have one‑way valves, forcing blood to travel in a closed loop.
The real reason he was mocked? He dared to replace a millennia‑old liver theory with a simple circular pump.
Ironically, the same “circulation” he proved later powered the very Royalist court that would exile him.

claims.claim: Harvey’s De Motu Cordis described blood moving in a circuit and faced strong opposition from physicians who preferred Galen’s liver theory.
Harvey’s publication caused his practice to suffer and he was mocked by other doctors.
Harvey used experiments on fish and serpents, and measured heart capacity and beats to show the amount of blood moved could not be produced by the liver.
Harvey’s discovery of one‑way venous valves explained why blood flows toward the heart.
